# Overview

`detectRUNS` detects genomic **Runs of Homozygosity (ROH)** and **Runs of Heterozygosity (ROHet)** in diploid organisms from SNP array data.  Version 1.0.0 is a major rewrite relative to the last CRAN release (0.9.6), introducing a compiled C++ BED engine, a redesigned S3 API, PLINK-compatible parameter semantics, and a suite of new analytical functions.

This document describes:

- What changed from CRAN version 0.9.6
- The internal architecture
- Algorithm details
- Full API reference
- Benchmark results and PLINK concordance validation
- Code audit findings and CRAN compliance status

---

# What Changed from CRAN 0.9.6

## Summary Table

| Category | CRAN 0.9.6 | detectRUNS 1.0.0 |
|---|---|---|
| Input format | PED/MAP only | **BED/BIM/FAM + PED/MAP** |
| Detection engine | Pure R (slow) | **C++ OpenMP (5–14× faster)** |
| Parallelism | R `mclapply` (PED only) | **OpenMP across chromosomes** |
| API entry point | `slidingRUNS.run()` / `consecutiveRUNS.run()` | **`scanRUNS()`** |
| Return value | Plain `data.frame` | **`RUNS` S3 object** |
| PLINK concordance | Partial (off-by-one length bug, wrong threshold/gap) | **100% exact match** |
| `runsIslands()` | Not available | **Permutation-based ROH island detection** |
| `reportRUNS()` | Not available | **HTML/Markdown/PDF report** |
| `runsAssociation()` | Not available | **Run–phenotype association** |
| Parallel `tableRuns()` | Single-threaded | **`mclapply` per chromosome** |
| `summaryRuns()` | Basic | **Per-class, per-chromosome Froh** |
| Test suite | 5 failures | **0 failures, 224 passing** |
| `R CMD check --as-cran` | Multiple ERRORs/WARNINGs | **0 ERRORs, 3 WARNINGs (vignette only)** |

## Key Bug Fixes

### Off-by-one in run length (PLINK concordance)

The most impactful correctness fix: PLINK computes run length as `end - start + 1` (inclusive); detectRUNS 0.9.6 computed `end - start` (exclusive). This caused runs at exactly `minLengthBps` to be silently dropped. Fixed in all four code paths:

| File | Function / path |
|------|----------------|
| `src/scan_roh.cpp` | BED consecutive (`emit_consec`) and BED sliding (`emit_sw`) |
| `src/rcpp_entry.cpp` | BED result extraction (`lengthBps`) |
| `src/functions.cpp` | PED consecutive (`consecutiveRunsCpp`) |
| `R/funktionen.R` | PED sliding (`createRUNdf`) |

### PLINK-compatible threshold semantics

The Bjelland sliding-window threshold was being applied as `>=` instead of `>`, causing marginal runs to differ from PLINK. Fixed to use strict `>`.

### PLINK-compatible maxGap semantics

Run-splitting on large gaps was applied per-window instead of once at the run level. Fixed by implementing exact run-level gap splitting in `createRUNdf()`.

### PED cross-chromosome boundary gaps

`diff(mapFile$bps)` generated large negative values at chromosome boundaries (last SNP of chr N vs first SNP of chr N+1). These were passed to the sliding window function as huge "gaps", incorrectly splitting runs. Fixed with `pmax(diff(map_df$bps), 0L)`.

# Architecture

│   ├── binary_runs.R     # saveRUNS() / loadRUNS() (binary .roh format)

# The BED Engine (C++)

## Overview

The BED engine replaces the pure-R sliding-window loop introduced in v0.9.6. It reads PLINK binary format directly, processes genotypes in packed 2-bit encoding, and distributes work across chromosomes using OpenMP.

## Key data structures

```cpp
// One parsed SNP from the BIM file
struct SnpInfo {
    int32_t  position;      // bp position
    uint8_t  chrom_idx;     // chromosome index (0-based)
};

// Running state for one individual during consecutive scan
struct ConsecState {
    bool     in_run;
    int32_t  run_start_bp, run_end_bp;
    int32_t  run_start_snp, run_end_snp;
    int32_t  n_opp, n_miss;
};

// One detected ROH record
struct RohRecord {
    int32_t  indiv_idx;
    int32_t  snp_start, snp_end;
    int32_t  start_bp, end_bp;
    int32_t  n_snps, n_opp, n_miss;
};
```

## Chromosome-parallel OpenMP strategy

The original v1.0 BED engine used a per-SNP parallelism pattern:

```
for each SNP j:
    #pragma omp single   ← barrier: read SNP row
    #pragma omp for      ← barrier: process individuals
```

This created **2 barriers × number of SNPs** — for a 777K-SNP dataset: ~155,000 synchronisation points, accounting for ~77 seconds of overhead regardless of data size.

Version 1.0 (this release) switches to **chromosome-level parallelism**:

```cpp
// Build chromosome ranges once
std::vector<ChromRange> chrom_ranges = build_chrom_ranges(bim);

// Thread-local storage: no sharing between threads
std::vector<std::vector<ConsecState>>    tl_states(n_threads, ...);
std::vector<std::vector<RohRecord>>      tl_rec(n_threads);
std::vector<std::vector<IndivSummary>>   tl_sum(n_threads, ...);
std::vector<std::vector<int32_t>>        tl_freq(n_threads, ...);

#pragma omp parallel num_threads(n_threads)
{
    const int tid = omp_get_thread_num();
    #pragma omp for schedule(dynamic, 1)
    for (int c = 0; c < n_chrom; ++c) {
        // Each thread owns its chromosome range entirely
        // No synchronisation needed during processing
        process_chromosome(c, tid, tl_rec[tid], tl_sum[tid], tl_freq[tid]);
    }
}

// Single sequential merge at the end
merge_thread_local_results(tl_rec, tl_sum, tl_freq);
```

**Benefits:**
- Zero synchronisation during scan (one merge at the very end)
- `schedule(dynamic, 1)` auto-balances unequal chromosome sizes
- Thread-local state avoids all race conditions

## BED file parsing

PLINK `.bed` files store genotypes as packed 2-bit values: 4 genotypes per byte.

```
Encoding:  00 = homozygous A1 (0)
           01 = missing    (NA)
           10 = heterozygous (1)
           11 = homozygous A2 (2)
```

`bed_reader.cpp` memory-maps the file and decodes one SNP row at a time:

```cpp
void decode_snp_row(const BedData& bed, int snp_idx, int8_t* out) {
    const int N     = bed.n_indiv;
    const int bytes = (N + 3) / 4;
    const uint8_t* row = bed.data.data() + 3 + (size_t)snp_idx * bytes;
    for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) {
        uint8_t bits = (row[i / 4] >> (2 * (i % 4))) & 0x3;
        out[i] = GENO_TABLE[bits];  // 0, 1, 2, or -1 (missing)
    }
}
```

# Algorithms

## Sliding Window (Bjelland et al. 2013)

For each SNP position $j$, a window of $W$ SNPs centred (or starting) at $j$ is evaluated. A window **passes** if:

$$\text{n\_opp}(j) \leq \text{maxOpp} \;\; \text{AND} \;\; \text{n\_miss}(j) \leq \text{maxMiss} \;\; \text{AND} \;\; \max(\text{gaps in window}) < \text{maxGap}$$

A SNP is in a ROH if the fraction of passing windows that cover it exceeds the threshold $\theta$:

$$\frac{\#\{\text{passing windows containing SNP } j\}}{\#\{\text{all windows containing SNP } j\}} > \theta$$

Contiguous SNPs in a ROH form a run. Post-filtering applies:

- `minSNP`: minimum SNPs in run
- `minLengthBps`: minimum `end - start + 1` (inclusive, PLINK-compatible)
- `minDensity`: minimum SNPs per kbp
- `maxOppRun`, `maxMissRun`: optional run-level het/missing caps

**BED engine note:** The sliding sum is maintained in O(1) per window step using a two-pointer technique, avoiding the O(W) recomputation present in the original R implementation.

## Consecutive Runs (Marras et al. 2015)

A run extends as long as consecutive SNPs satisfy:

$$\text{geno}(j) = \text{target} \;\; \text{OR} \;\; \text{geno}(j) = \text{miss} \;\; (\text{up to maxMiss accumulated})$$
$$\text{AND} \;\; \text{gap}(j-1, j) < \text{maxGap}$$

A run ends when an opposite-type genotype is encountered (up to `maxOpp` tolerated) or when a gap exceeds `maxGap`. At each chromosome boundary, all running states are reset.

Post-filtering is identical to the sliding-window method.

# API Reference

## `scanRUNS()` — Main Entry Point

```r
scanRUNS(
  genoFile,                          # .bed, .ped, or base name
  bimFile  = NULL,                   # BED only; inferred if NULL
  famFile  = NULL,                   # BED only; inferred if NULL
  mapFile  = NULL,                   # PED only; inferred if NULL
  method   = c("consecutive","sliding"),
  ROHet    = FALSE,                  # TRUE = detect ROHet
  minSNP   = 3,                      # min SNPs in run
  maxOpp   = 1,                      # max opposite genotypes (window)
  maxMiss  = 1,                      # max missing genotypes (window)
  minLengthBps = 1000,               # min run length in bp (inclusive)
  maxGap   = 1e6,                    # max gap between consecutive SNPs
  windowSize  = 15,                  # window size (sliding only)
  threshold   = 0.05,                # Bjelland threshold (sliding only)
  minDensity  = 1/1000,              # min SNPs per kbp
  maxOppRun   = NULL,                # max het in entire run (sliding only)
  maxMissRun  = NULL,                # max missing in entire run (sliding only)
  nThreads    = NULL,                # NULL = auto-detect physical cores
  verbose     = TRUE
)
```

**Returns:** A `RUNS` S3 object with elements:

| Element | Type | Description |
|---------|------|-------------|
| `$runs` | `data.table` | One row per run: `group, id, chrom, nSNP, from, to, lengthBps` |
| `$summary` | `data.table` | Per-individual: `group, id, n_ROH, total_length_bp, mean_length, n_snps_in_roh` |
| `$snp_freq` | `integer` vector | Count of individuals with ROH at each SNP (BED only) |
| `$chrom_map` | `integer` named vector | Chromosome name → internal index (BED only) |
| `$scan_params` | `list` | All parameters used for provenance |

## `summaryRuns()` — Froh and ROH Statistics

```r
summaryRuns(
  runs,             # RUNS object or data.frame
  mapFile = NULL,   # needed for Froh calculation
  Class   = 1,      # Mbp class size (1, 2, 4, 8 Mbp)
  snpInRuns = FALSE # include per-SNP run frequency (slow)
)
```

Returns a named list with Froh genome-wide, per-chromosome, and per-length-class breakdowns.

## `tableRuns()` — Most Common ROH Regions

```r
tableRuns(
  runs      = NULL,
  SnpInRuns = NULL,
  genotypeFile = NULL,
  mapFile   = NULL,
  threshold = 0.5,              # min fraction of individuals
  nCores    = detectCores()     # parallel chromosome processing
)
```

Returns a `data.frame` with one row per common ROH region per population.

## `runsIslands()` — Permutation-Based Island Detection

```r
runsIslands(
  runs,
  bed_path,
  percentile = 0.99,    # empirical percentile threshold
  n_perm     = 1000,    # number of permutations
  method     = "sliding",
  nThreads   = NULL,
  seed       = NULL,
  ...                   # scanRUNS parameters
)
```

Identifies genomic regions where ROH accumulate across individuals significantly more than expected by chance, using a permutation null distribution. Implements the approach of Falchi et al. (2026).

## `runsAssociation()` — Run–Phenotype Association

```r
runsAssociation(
  runs,
  phenoFile,           # tab-separated: id, phenotype [, covariates]
  method   = "glm",
  minCarriers = 5      # min individuals carrying run
)
```

Fits a linear/logistic model per ROH region and returns association statistics.

## `reportRUNS()` — Automated Report

```r
reportRUNS(
  runs,
  output_file = "detectRUNS_report",
  output_format = "html",     # "html", "markdown", "pdf"
  include_plots = TRUE,
  include_islands = FALSE,
  ...
)
```

Generates a self-contained report with run statistics, Froh tables, Manhattan plots, and (optionally) ROH islands.

## `saveRUNS()` / `loadRUNS()`

```r
saveRUNS(runs, file)   # saves to binary .roh format (preserves full RUNS object)
loadRUNS(file)         # restores RUNS object with all metadata
```

## Deprecated Functions (still exported for backward compatibility)

| Old function | Replacement |
|---|---|
| `slidingRUNS.run()` | `scanRUNS(..., method = "sliding")` |
| `consecutiveRUNS.run()` | `scanRUNS(..., method = "consecutive")` |
| `saveROH()` | `saveRUNS()` |
| `loadROH()` | `loadRUNS()` |
| `as_ROH()` | `as_RUNS()` |
| `rohIslands()` | `runsIslands()` |

# Parameter Guide

## PLINK Equivalence Table

| detectRUNS parameter | PLINK flag | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `minSNP` | `--homozyg-snp` | Min SNPs in ROH |
| `minLengthBps` | `--homozyg-kb` × 1000 | Min length in bp |
| `maxGap` | `--homozyg-gap` × 1000 | Max gap in bp |
| `windowSize` | `--homozyg-window-snp` | Window size |
| `maxOpp` | `--homozyg-window-het` | Max het in window |
| `maxMiss` | `--homozyg-window-missing` | Max missing in window |
| `threshold` | `--homozyg-window-threshold` | Coverage fraction |
| `minDensity` | `1 / --homozyg-density` | SNPs per kbp |

## Default vs PLINK Default

| Parameter | detectRUNS default | PLINK default |
|---|---|---|
| `minSNP` | 3 | 100 |
| `minLengthBps` | 1,000 | 1,000,000 |
| `maxGap` | 1,000,000 | 1,000,000 |
| `windowSize` | 15 | 50 |
| `maxOpp` | 1 | 1 |
| `maxMiss` | 1 | 5 |
| `threshold` | 0.05 | 0.05 |
| `minDensity` | 0.001 | 0.02 |

Note: detectRUNS defaults are intentionally permissive. For PLINK-equivalent results use `minLengthBps = 500000, minSNP = 15, minDensity = 1/50`.

df <- data.frame(
  Dataset    = c("suini_12 (pig)", "SELMOL (cattle)"),
  SNPs       = c("54,089", "44,191"),
  Ind        = c("1,208", "4,095"),
  PLINK_time = c("0.38s", "0.95s"),
  DR_1T      = c("2.00s", "5.03s"),

  DR_RSS_14T = c("274 MB", "450 MB"),
  Runs       = c("536,964", "1,274,826"),

## Parameter Sweep — PLINK Concordance

50 parameter combinations tested against PLINK on a 1,000-individual SELMOL subset (44,191 SNPs, 29 chromosomes).

```{r param-sweep, echo=FALSE}
df3 <- data.frame(
  Section   = c("One-at-a-time sweep (40 combos)", "Extreme combinations (10 combos)", "Total"),
  Tested    = c(40, 10, 50),
  PASS      = c(40, 10, 50),
  Match_pct = c("100%", "100%", "100%")
)
knitr::kable(df3, caption = "BED sliding window vs PLINK --homozyg concordance")
```

Parameters swept individually and in extreme combinations:

| Parameter | Values tested |
|---|---|
| `minSNP` | 3, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30 |
| `maxOpp` | 0, 1, 2, 3 |
| `maxMiss` | 0, 1, 2, 3 |
| `maxGap` | 100K, 500K, 1M, 2M, 5M, 10M |
| `windowSize` | 5, 10, 15, 20, 30 |
| `threshold` | 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 0.30, 0.50 |
| `minLengthBps` | 100K, 250K, 500K, 1M, 2M |
| `minDensity` | 1/50, 1/100, 1/500, 1/1000, 1/5000 |

Extreme combinations included `all_lenient` (606K runs, tiny windows, many hets), `all_strict` (10K runs, large windows, no hets), boundary tests at exactly 500K and 1M bp, and high-heterozygosity stress tests.

# Code Audit Findings

## Audit scope

All R files (12 files, ~4,400 lines) and C++ files (8 files, ~3,300 lines) were reviewed line-by-line. Findings are categorised by severity.

## Fixed in this release

| Severity | Finding | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Critical | Off-by-one run length (PLINK discordance) | `end - start + 1` in 5 locations |
| Critical | Wrong threshold semantics (`>=` vs `>`) | Changed to strict `>` |
| Critical | Wrong maxGap semantics (window vs run level) | Run-level gap split in `createRUNdf()` |
| Critical | PED cross-chromosome negative gaps | `pmax(..., 0L)` |
| High | 5 pre-existing test failures | Fixed `snpInsideRunsCpp` signature, tableRuns threshold validation, deprecated error strings |
| High | ggplot2 `size=` deprecation | Replaced with `linewidth=` |
| High | Missing `@import ggplot2` | Added; resolved runtime errors in plot functions |
| Medium | Rd files missing new params | `devtools::document()` regenerated all 34 Rd files |
| Medium | Undocumented deprecated exports | Added roxygen docs with `@keywords internal` |
| Medium | Non-portable Makevars (GNU extensions) | Replaced with `$(SHLIB_OPENMP_CXXFLAGS)` |
| Low | `tableRuns` spawns too many cores under CRAN check | Cap at 2 when `_R_CHECK_LIMIT_CORES_` is set |
| Low | Typo: "doesn't exists" | "doesn't exist" |
| Low | Missing `LazyData` in DESCRIPTION | Added `LazyData: false` |

## Remaining known issues

| Severity | Finding | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Medium | Vignette not pre-built (`inst/doc/` empty) | Deferred — needs `devtools::build_vignettes()` |
| Low | Column naming inconsistency (`nSNP` vs `COUNT` vs `n_snps_in_roh`) | Design decision from API redesign; documented |
| Low | No progress bar when OpenMP is enabled | By design — per-SNP progress incompatible with chromosome-parallel |
| Low | `pdflatex` not available locally | System toolchain; CRAN servers have it |
| Low | HTML tidy version too old for `--as-cran` | System toolchain |

# New Features in Detail

## `runsIslands()` — ROH Islands

Implements the permutation approach of Falchi et al. (2026). For each chromosome, the observed SNPROH count (number of individuals with a ROH covering each SNP) is compared against an empirical null distribution generated by randomly permuting run labels across individuals. SNPs exceeding the `percentile` threshold form "islands."

```r
res  <- scanRUNS("mydata.bed", method = "sliding", minLengthBps = 500000)
isls <- runsIslands(res, bed_path = "mydata.bed",
                    percentile = 0.99, n_perm = 1000)
print(isls)    # summary of islands per chromosome
plot(isls)     # Manhattan-style plot
summary(isls)  # island SNP counts, thresholds
```

## `runsAssociation()` — Run–Phenotype Association

Fits a GLM (linear or logistic) for each ROH region with the phenotype as outcome. ROH carrier status (1/0) is the predictor. Returns beta coefficients, SE, and p-values.

```r
assoc <- runsAssociation(res, phenoFile = "pheno.txt",
                         method = "glm", minCarriers = 10)
```

## `reportRUNS()` — Automated Report

Generates a self-contained HTML (or Markdown/PDF) report including:
- Scan parameters and dataset metadata
- Run count, length distribution, Froh statistics per population
- Manhattan plot (% SNPs in ROH)
- tableRuns output (most common ROH regions)
- Violin plots of ROH length distribution by class
- Optional: ROH islands

```r
reportRUNS(res, output_file = "my_roh_report", output_format = "html")
```
